Partnership Vision - Stronger Together
Who Are We?
We are a federation based in Tower Hamlets, currently comprising of 2 Primary Schools and 1 Secondary School.
Committed to educational excellence, we are a values-driven organisation, underpinned by our vision that schools are ‘Stronger Together in Partnership.’
As a Federation we are proud of the unique traditions that have shaped our 3 exceptional schools, Hague Primary, Stewart Headlam Primary and Swanlea Secondary, but also of the value of partnership which has allowed us to share strengths and grow together. We have achieved much in terms of Quality of Education, Curriculum Development, Teaching & Learning, Leadership Development, Cultural Capital & Enrichment and building Sustainable School Systems.
Weavers Federation - Our Shared Heritage
Weavers Field is the green heart of our community - where families play, socialise, and connect.​ But it's also our history. From the 1700 to 1900s, the Huguenot silk weavers lived and worked - migrants who brought extraordinary skill to the East End textile industry. Brick Lane and Spitalfields are known for links to the textile industry and which many of our current Bangladeshi families have historic connections. ​1000s of children attended our schools formerly known as:
These schools each had 1200 - 1500 pupils. ​
Then and now, our community is built by people bringing their strengths together. In silk weaving, individual threads - no matter how beautiful - are fragile alone.​ But when you weave them together - warp and weft - they create something strong, resilient, and valuable.​
That's us, it started with the primaries and grew - 3 headteachers, Cathy Gillespie, Judy Knappett and Brenda Landers in an area of following roles, our Federation grows​. Woven together, we're stronger, more sustainable, and better able to ensure excellence thrives across both schools.
Federation is the flattest equitable partnership structure for school leadership built on trusting relationships​.​
Our Mission
Our Values
To inspire all our children to have a love of learning so that they strive to achieve and be successful in doing so.
To provide a stimulating, progressive curriculum which offers enrichment opportunities for all children respecting their rights, responsibilities and individuality.
To take pride in our unique schools, celebrating each school’s traditions whilst growing in partnership to develop a new shared learning culture.
Choosing to do the right things, based on wisdom, research and values, even when it’s hard or no-one is looking so that we have trust between us and the community.

Our Federation Journey
February 2025
Federation Governors’ Learning Walk at Hague and Stewart Headlam. Secondary and primary committee governors listening to pupils, staff and parents’ voices on the quality of education.
September - December 2024
Governors from Stewart Headlam and Hague Primary Schools and Governors from Swanlea Secondary School consulted parents and staff about a new federation partnership between the three schools.
September 2024 – Alison Goodliffe appointed New Head
Alison Goodliffe, appointed New Head of School at Hague as Sue Walsh retired.
April 2024 – Swanlea Ofsted: OUTSTANDING
January 2024 – Weavers Federation formed
‘Stronger Together’ – There are many excellent benefits of our schools working together with governors and staff. It means we are ‘stronger together through partnership’ more able to face the challenges of running schools successfully. We are the first primary and secondary hard federation in Tower Hamlets. We are weaving strands of our leadership, governance and transition Y6 to Y7 curriculum together so that we shine as outstanding schools, serving the local community.
July 2023 – Stewart Headlam Ofsted: OUTSTANDING
September 2022 – Hague Ofsted: GOOD
September 2022
Established a single site federation nursery class for Stewart Headlam and Hague pupils based at Hague. It has been a great use of our resources and talented teaching teams.
March 2022 – Stewart Headlam Ofsted: GOOD
January 2021
Shared leadership strategy after Cathy retired. One Executive Headteacher – Judy Knappett, formerly Headteacher at Hague working across the two schools with Heads of School; Nilufar Chowdhury at Stewart Headlam and Sue Walsh at Hague. The primary federation partnership and strategic planning helped the schools to address local and national education challenges of falling rolls and education during Covid pandemic years.
Primary Federation and shared leadership helped our schools to be sustainable and address the issue of falling rolls in the west of Tower Hamlets. Stewart Headlam started a journey of transitioning from 2FE to 1FE by 2025.
January 2020 – SHH Federation established
Two primaries hard federated with one shared governing body and two Headteachers; Cathy Gillespie Headteacher at Stewart Headlam and Judy Knappett Headteacher at Hague had a vision of the two schools being, ‘Stronger through partnership’ to provide the best education for our community in challenging times.
Stewart Headlam Primary School | Tapp Street, London, E1 5RE
Hague Primary School | Wilmot Street, London, E2 0BP

pageCache.text:
What do governing bodies do?
Governors are the strategic leaders of our school and have a vital role to play in making sure every child gets the best possible education.
Governing bodies should have a strong focus on three core strategic functions:
Ensuring clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction
Governing bodies are the key strategic decision-making body of every school. It is their role to set the school's strategic framework and to ensure all statutory duties are met.
The governing body should ensure that the school has a medium to long-term vision for its future. The governing body should also ensure that there is a robust strategy in place for achieving its vision. This strategy should address the fundamental questions of where are we now, where do we want to be, and how are we going to get there.
The governing body should set and safeguard a school ethos of high expectations of everyone in the school community. This includes high expectations for the behaviour, progress and attainment of all pupils in the school, and for the conduct and professionalism of both staff and governors.
Holding the Headteacher to account for the educational performance of the school and its pupils, and the performance management of staff
Governing bodies should work to support and strengthen the leadership of the Headteacher, and hold them to account for the day-to-day running of the school, including the performance management of teachers. Governing bodies should play a strategic role, and avoid routine involvement in operational matters. It should focus strongly on holding the Headteacher to account for exercising her professional judgement in these matters and of all their other duties.
Overseeing the financial performance of the school and making sure its money is well spent Governing bodies are responsible for making sure their school's money is well spent.
They should do this by making sure they have at least one governor with specific skills and experience of financial matters, and by asking questions such as:
The governing body helps to set, and keep under review, the broad framework within which the headteacher and staff run the school. In all its work, the governing body focuses on the key issues of raising standards of achievement, establishing high expectations and promoting effective teaching and learning.

Welcome to Stewart Headlam Primary School
Message from the Head of School
Welcome to the Stewart Headlam School Website. We hope that you can use it to find information you need to know or simply to show off what’s happening to your family and friends. For new visitors we hope that it gives you a view to learning and life at Stewart Headlam.
It is an absolute pleasure and privilege to be the Head of School of this warm, friendly and welcoming school. Stewart Headlam is a primary school that serves children from 3 to 11 years. We were a two form entry school but are currently reducing to a one form of entry, with some upper KS2 classes still being two form. We are located in a multicultural community, situated between bustling Whitechapel and Bethnal Green, the heart of London’s East End. Ever since Stewart Headlam opened its doors in the late 19th century, pupils have been and are at the heart of everything we do.
We want all of our children to be happy, healthy and enjoy learning. We make every effort to ensure children at Stewart Headlam get the best opportunities we can offer. Our curriculum is designed to be relevant to the children and engage, inspire and elevate children’s knowledge and understanding.
Nilufar Chowdhury Head of School
